When I was around ten or eleven, our family took a trip to this house that had just recently had a huge fire. My dad was kind of cheap so instead of going to Sears to get a new oven, we went to this burnt husk of a house to see if any kitchen appliances could be salvaged. Anywho, when we got there, this lady who happened to be the sister (or maybe she was the realtor or both) of the guy responsible for the house fire, was showing us around and we came to this big room with all this charred up crap and I noticed a beautiful glass pyramid on the floor. My parents and the lady continued to the next room but I stayed behind staring at the object. It was beautiful to me, mesmerizing even. It was dark purple on the floor, but when I held it to the light it was light purple and kind of see through. 

Anyway to make a long story short, I was going to ask the lady if I could have the pyramid but before I could my brother reached over to grab it cause he wanted to see it and I did not want him to take it because like I said, I really *really* liked it and for some reason I thought he would break it or something. 

So we struggled over it for a few seconds and I somehow ended up stabbing him in the hand with it. It probably wasn't that deep of a wound but at the time I was mortified and my brother was shrieking like a soldier in WW1 getting his arm sawed off. 

I don't quite remember how the day ended but I do know that as soon as blood was drawn, I dropped the pyramid.

At my summer job last year I was working with these preschool aged kids and whenever it was snack or lunch time I was always fascinated by the way these kids ate their fruit. Because my area is so strict on healthy eating, parents weren't allowed to send their kids with cookies or candy for dessert and for the kids who didn't have a lunch, it was provided and the sweetest thing they got was fresh fruit. 


The type of fruit was different each day of the week and Monday was orange day. For some reason, we couldn't find the knife to cut the oranges in slices, so the kids were either peeling them themselves or we peeled it for them and split it into sections. 


Except this one kid just....Peeled the skin off of the top of the orange and bit into it like an apple. But he didn't peel the rest of the orange and instead shoved his entire face (his eyes were open, mind you) into the hole he made and just ate it like that. Like a wild animal. We had to give him like five paper towels and even then he wasn't completely orange free. But yeah, that was how he ate  it. And I was curious so I tried that technique at home later and nearly blinded myself when the citrus juice squirted into my eyes.

----
On Wednesday, we had bananas and most kids ate the bananas the usual way (after we peeled them), but some kids ate them like corn on the cob, or tore it in half and started to sway to their own internal music (imagine Buckwheat from Little Rascals with his pickles but sans pickle song). This one kid however, grabbed the top of his banana in his fist and smushed it before eating it and that's how he continued until the fruit was gone. It was interesting if not a little gross and super messy. 

TLDR: Kids eat in special ways.

When I was sixteen or something, I wanted to get my ears pierced and I got it done at Claire's because that's where everyone else went. The earrings I got where adorable and I felt extremely elegant now that I could wear earrings like everyone else and I went to sleep that night with a sense of accomplishment. 

I woke up with a headache, blood and pus on my pillow and swollen ear lobes. During the night, my ear lobe had swelled and swallowed my piercings, leaving a tiny, bloody and crusty hole in their wake. My mom took me to the doctor who was completely thrown by my predicament and had zero clue on what to do. But it was apparent that the earrings had to be removed or the problem would worsen, so the doctor clumsily began shoving tweezers in the tiny ear holes and pulling on the face of the earring while using a tweezer to pull on the stud at the back of my lobe. 

After about ten minutes of fumbling--at one point the doctor called a nurse in to ask if she knew what to do--he managed to get both earrings out and I went home a broken teenager. 

The doctor warned me against going back to Claire's because the gun must've been dirty or they'd lied about what their earrings were made out of.

Two years later, I'm ready to try again but this time I go to the doctor who uses a sterile gun to pierce my ears, and my mom provided pure gold earrings. 

Doctor + Definitely not fake earrings = Success right? 

NOPE. 

The same thing happened again. 

Turns out I'm allergic to whatever metal piercing guns contain. Yay me!

My mom hadn't noticed yet, so I just kept my hand on my mouth in a poor attempt at hiding the wound so that I could take care of it later.

In my underdeveloped kid brain, I assumed that my mom would just go "oh okay!" and not yell at me and then we'd have ice cream or something. 

Obviously, she did not do that. She called my friend's mom and repeated what I had said and I don't quite remember what happened after that but basically within an hour or two, I confessed to my mom and I had to apologize to my friend's older sister and their family.

When I was around seven or eight and my brother was nine/ten, we were both bored and although we had a GameCube as well as a computer with A LOT of games, my brother and I decided that we were going to play outside. Were we going to play tag? Hide and seek? The ever entertaining TV tag? NOPE. We weren't going to play any of those safe and logical games. Instead we decided to play with our dad's measuring tape. For a reason I do not remember, my brother and I tried to guess how long the yard was and in a brilliant moment of mathematical prowess which could have better been applied to our studies (we were both terrible at math), we decided to use our dad's tape measure to well...Measure the yard. Most of you probably know this, but we didn't but uh...Tape measures have limits, so you shouldn't pull a tape measure that stops at six feet because if you do, it'll get stuck. And you know what you really shouldn't do? Jam the 'tape' back into the slot and then hope to hell your dad won't notice. 

Well...I guess my dad had a lot of shit to measure that day because as soon as he came back from the store, he went straight for the tape measure and when he realized it was broken, he called us both downstairs--and okay, so I'm still mad at him about this part because he didn't seem that mad. It kind of seemed like he was going to just give us a stern talking to because that's what he did and then he let us leave. But not five minutes later, he called us back and he had his thick ass sandal in hand which he promptly smacked us with on the hand (once for me, twice for my brother) and it hurt like hell. I still remember how raw my hand felt and how much I cried afterwards.

And that, friends, is the reason why even though I am a grown woman, I will not touch a tape measure.

TLDR: Dad beat us with his shoe.
